title: Microsoft 365 admin center: set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN
summary: The setup choice, administrator roles, licensing statements and controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The briefing correctly distinguishes the documented setup experience from the roadmap's still-in-development status and past target month.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-17T23:00:45.
Microsoft plans to let administrators set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.
claims.quote: We are updating the Brand Center setup experience so that administrators can set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.

claims.claim: According to the roadmap description, Public CDN has been enabled during setup even for organisations needing only governance capabilities.
claims.quote: Today, Public CDN is enabled as part of Brand Center setup, even when an organization only wants to use branding governance capabilities that do not require it.

claims.claim: The planned change lets organisations defer Public CDN until they need dependent capabilities such as organisational fonts.
claims.quote: With this update, organizations can begin using Brand Center while deferring Public CDN until they need capabilities that depend on it, such as organizational fonts.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn already documents a choice to enable the public Office 365 CDN during Brand Center setup.
claims.quote: During setup, you can choose whether to enable the Office 365 Content Delivery Network (CDN), a public content delivery network (public CDN).

claims.claim: Brand fonts require Public CDN because it hosts their font files.
claims.quote: This public CDN is required for brand fonts because it hosts the font files.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Brand colours and other Brand Center capabilities do not require Public CDN.
claims.quote: Brand colors and the other brand center capabilities don't require a public CDN

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn gives three setup scenarios: no organisation assets, organisation assets with private CDN, and organisation assets with public CDN.
claims.quote:
Scenario 1: Your tenant doesn't currently use the SharePoint organization assets feature.
- Scenario 2: Your tenant uses the SharePoint organization assets feature with a private CDN.
- Scenario 3: Your tenant uses the SharePoint organization assets feature with a public CDN.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For the no-assets and private-CDN setup scenarios, Public CDN (optional) is turned off by default.
claims.quote: Under Public CDN (optional), choose whether to enable the public CDN now. Enable Public CDN (optional) if you plan to use brand fonts. The option is turned off by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Public CDN can be enabled later if it was deferred during setup.
claims.quote: If you defer Public CDN during setup and later want to use brand fonts, a Global Administrator can enable Public CDN from the brand center settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: For tenants already using organisation assets with public CDN, Public CDN is already enabled and no additional CDN action is required.
claims.quote: For this scenario, the public CDN is already enabled, so no additional CDN action is required.

claims.claim: The setup control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Brand center > Public CDN (optional).
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to Settings > Org settings.
2. Select Brand center.
3. Enter a name for the brand center site, such as Brand Guide.
4. Under Public CDN (optional), choose whether to enable the public CDN now.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled -CdnType Public -Enable $true enables the tenant's Public CDN.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled -CdnType public -Enable $true

The example enables a CDN.

claims.claim: The CDN cmdlet enables or disables Public CDN at tenant scope.
claims.quote: Enables or disables Public content delivery network (CDN) or Private CDN on the tenant level.

claims.claim: Learn assigns Brand Center setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center to a Global Administrator.
claims.quote: To enable the brand center, a Global Administrator completes a few steps in the Microsoft 365 admin center to create or activate the brand center app.

claims.claim: The capability is admin-opt-in: an administrator must configure Brand Center and choose Public CDN enablement.
claims.quote: For this scenario, a Global Administrator creates the brand center app:

claims.claim: This SharePoint setup option uses the product's included licensing model rather than a separately documented entitlement.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: SharePoint access requires an assigned licence that includes SharePoint.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Brand Center overview names no licence specific to Brand Center or its optional Public CDN setup choice.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Brand Center licensing license requirements optional Public CDN Brand center setup. Read brand-center-overview in full and SharePoint service-description licensing text; overview names E3/E5 for PowerPoint fonts, not a separate setup licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Customers with E3 or E5 licenses can use Organization Font Support in PowerPoint for the web to edit and display their fonts.
claims.quote: Customers with E3 or E5 licenses can take advantage of Organization Font Support in PowerPoint for the web to edit and display their fonts.

claims.claim: Office 365 CDN is included as part of the SharePoint Online subscription.
claims.quote: The Office 365 CDN service is included as part of your SharePoint Online subscription.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Publishing brand fonts creates font catalog files stored publicly alongside the fonts and accessible outside the organisation to anyone with their URLs.
claims.quote:
The newly created font catalog files are publicly stored, along with the fonts, in the cloud
The files are accessible to anyone, even people outside of your organization, who can get the URLs that link to them.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to use the font feature if the fonts contain proprietary information.
claims.quote: Don't use this feature if your fonts contain proprietary information

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to use the font feature where font licence restrictions prohibit uses such as cloud hosting.
claims.quote: or if they have license usage restrictions, such as restrictions on cloud hosting

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to use the font feature if the organisation is uncomfortable making the fonts public.
claims.quote: or your organization isn't comfortable making the fonts publicly available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Brand Center site permissions control app access, and site owners can use the app.
claims.quote: you can control who can access the brand center app by customizing the site permissions of the brand center site. Site owners of the brand center site will be able to use the brand center app.

claims.claim: Brand managers with access to the app can upload and manage brand assets.
claims.quote: Within the app itself, the brand managers are able to upload and manage their organization’s brand assets.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Brand managers cannot add fonts until a Global Administrator enables Public CDN.
claims.quote: If Public CDN isn't enabled, a Global Administrator must enable it before brand managers can add fonts.

claims.claim: Each additional geography wanting custom fonts needs an organisation asset library in a site using Public CDN.
claims.quote: Each additional geography where custom fonts are wanted must have an organization asset library set up in a site that uses the Public CDN.

claims.claim: Only one Brand Center is allowed per organisation.
claims.quote: The SharePoint brand center currently only allows one brand center for your organization

claims.claim: The Brand Center app is created in the tenant's primary geo.
claims.quote: The SharePoint brand center currently only creates a single brand center app in the primary geo of a tenant.

claims.claim: The Public CDN choice does not change existing SharePoint organisation assets library and template library configuration.
claims.quote: this choice doesn't change how your existing SharePoint organization assets library and template libraries are configured.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a setup change without specifying an action for tenants that already set up Brand Center.
claims.quote: We are updating the Brand Center setup experience so that administrators can set up Brand Center without enabling Public CDN.

claims.claim: The roadmap item describes a setup choice rather than an agent or automated action.
claims.quote: organizations can begin using Brand Center while deferring Public CDN until they need capabilities that depend on it, such as organizational fonts.

claims.claim: Learn does not say that the Brand Center setup option calls Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center enable Public CDN after setup brand center settings Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled licensing. Read brand-center-overview, Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled and CDN Quickstart; no passage specifies the setup option's implementation.

claims.claim: Learn names Brand Center settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center for later enablement without a more detailed later-enablement path.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center enable Public CDN after setup brand center settings Set-SPOTenantCdnEnabled licensing. Read brand-center-overview setup and management sections; later enablement is described only as from brand center settings.

claims.claim: A Global Administrator must create or activate Brand Center before people can use its app.
claims.quote: To enable the brand center, a Global Administrator completes a few steps in the Microsoft 365 admin center to create or activate the brand center app.

claims.claim: The Brand Center management documentation places site-permissions management in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: SharePoint site owners and above can update the site permissions in the SharePoint Admin Center such as adding more brand managers to the experience.
